title: OpenXR depth submission broken when using MSAA with Forward+
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduceable in all versions, including 4.6

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.mrlink3.mono (3993b4005) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 127.7 GiB memory

### Issue description


There is currently a bug when using OpenXR with "Submit Depth Buffer" enabled while MSAA is enabled with the Forward+ renderer. The issue is that RendererViewport will use `texture_storage->render_target_set_override` to set overrides for the color and depth buffers for the renderer to render into. Without MSAA, this is fine because the color/depth textures are created externally by the OpenXR runtime and they have the correct usage flags to render into. But with MSAA enabled, Forward+ uses special compute resolve shaders and thus required `STORAGE` usage which the OpenXR module does not enable. The OpenXR module doesn't know whether to create a depth swapchain for `STORAGE` or `DEPTH_STENCIL` because it doesn't know whether the override will result in being resolved into (requiring `STORAGE`) or rendered directly into (requiring `DEPTH_STENCIL`).
I have investigated a number of solutions:

1. Modify the OpenXR module to create depth textures with the `COMPUTE` `usage_flag` base on if the viewport has MSAA enabled for 3D. This would also be specific for Forward+ since the mobile renderer has worked around this problem (for Vulkan only) by using a Vulkan resolve feature that allows it to natively resolve depth textures. I've identified two ways this can be done:
   1.  Simple way: Key off the project settings to determine if MSAA is enabled. The flaw is this breaks if the application toggles MSAA dynamically (my product built on Godot will do this because we will have different rendering quality settings).
   2. Complicated way: Look up the current MSAA setting for the viewport or render target and recreate `XrSwapchains` as needed with compatible usage flags. The OpenXR module is passed the `render_target` `RID`, so additional plumbing is needed so that `RenderTarget` can expose the MSAA 3D setting (it already exposes the MSAA 2D setting).
        1. My prototype implementation is here: https://github.com/brycehutchings/godot/pull/6
2. Create raster shader equivalents of the depth resolve compute shaders and pick based on the render target. There actually are already raster equivalent shaders for depth resolve that are available and currently going unused. The problem is the `VOXEL_GI_RESOLVE` variant which would have to be reworked as a raster shader, and I haven't looked into if that is feasible. I presume compute shaders are used for a reason though, otherwise if Forward+ could migrate to raster shaders then that also solves the problem and avoids forked logic.
3. Add support for other graphics APIs to support depth resolve (like D3D12). I have actually implemented this as well, and found it does not work because D3D12 is stricter than Vulkan and doesn't like resolving from a depth buffer with a stencil aspect to a depth buffer without stencil.
4. Have Forward+ ignore the depth override if it is incompatible and do a blit at the end. Presumably this has some extra overhead though.

I have prototypes of 1a, 1b, 2 (without support for GI resolve though), and 3 (which ended up not working). For my team's product, 1b is what I plan to use because we need the dynamic support and it brings parity to Unity which we were using before, but I can contribute any of 1a/1b/2 if any of them are in the direction that the Godot maintainers would prefer.



### Steps to reproduce

Using a minimal XR project on PC with Forward+ renderer, enable "Submit Depth Buffer" and use a runtime that supports it. Observe that the submitted texture is always 0'd.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[xr-msaa.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25423201/xr-msaa.zip)

This will use GDScript to toggle MSAA 3D on/off every 2 seconds. It has OpenXR enabled, Depth Submission enabled, and uses Forward+.
